title: Grateful Dead Live at Winterland Arena on 1971-03-24
lineage: SBD > Master Reel (7.5ips 1/4 Track) > Master Dat (48k) > Dat (Sony R500) > SEK'D Prodif Plus > Samplitude v7.02 Professional > FLAC16

ai_review.summary: Excellent soundboard capture of a high‑energy spring ’71 show featuring a smoking Hard To Handle and rare King Bee, with crisp audio and standout performances.
ai_review.review: The recording delivers a clear, full‑show soundboard mix that showcases the band’s hot spring‑1971 vibe. Highlights include an early‑version Bertha, a blistering Hard To Handle solo exchange between Jerry and Phil, a rare King Bee, and a thrilling Truckin > Drums > Other One sequence. The audio is clean with a characteristic heavy‑bass low end, making the performance very enjoyable.

ai_rating.rationale: Most reviewers rate the show and recording highly (5‑star), praising both musical moments and sound quality; only one moderate rating tempers the average slightly.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Full‑show board mix, clear and balanced with a heavy ’71‑era bass presence; no major dropouts or muddiness reported.

show_quality.setlist_flow: Complete, mostly in order set; reviewers note the show flows strongly with high energy throughout and a particularly tight second‑set sequence.

band_member_comments.Jerry: His solo on Hard To Handle is described as intense, with expressive string bends and classic 1971 tone.
band_member_comments.Phil: Heavy bass noted; praised for climbing the fretboard, intense chording, and a standout jam that pre‑figures later B A D F# motifs.
band_member_comments.Bob: Vocals (Pig Pen) are "right on" and Bob Weir’s solo is called one of his best, adding to the song’s impact.
band_member_comments.Drums: The Drum segment within Truckin>Drums>Other One is highlighted as a pleasure, contributing to the show’s momentum.
